claims.claim: A linear optimal power dispatch on the GB 20-node network can be solved to optimality with PyPSA + HiGHS for the 168-hour week.
Base scenario weekly system operating cost is ~£710 M.
Tightening transmission to 50% (S1) increases curtailment and total cost.
claims.evidence: scenario_summary.csv: S1 cost = 8.05e8 vs S0 7.10e8; curtail 2.87 TWh vs 2.24 TWh

claims.claim: +50% wind capacity (S2) lowers cost but increases curtailment.
claims.evidence: scenario_summary.csv: S2 cost = 6.81e8 (-4%); curtailment 4.14 TWh (+85%) vs base

claims.claim: Removing storage (S3) does not change total cost meaningfully because backstop sets the price most of the time.
claims.evidence: scenario_summary.csv: S3 vs S0 objective = 7.1027e8 vs 7.1027e8 (matched); per-bus dispatch identical.

claims.claim: Tripling gas marginal cost (S4) almost completely drives gas out of the merit order.
claims.evidence: scenario_summary.csv: gas_MWh drops from 1.35 TWh to 0 in S4.

claims.claim: A wind drought (cf x 0.5, S5) is the only scenario where the modelled PHS storage is meaningfully cycled.
claims.evidence: report/images/fig_storage_soc.png; outputs/storage_soc_S5_wind_drought.csv contains non-zero SoC traces while S0/S1/S2/S4 SoC remain ~0.

claims.claim: Transmission utilisation is high in S1 (mean ~82%, peak 100%), indicating widespread congestion.
